sources.title: OOP with Java Lecture Notes (Prof. K. Menon)
Modern Java: Objects and Beyond, 2nd Ed.

classes_and_objects.name: Classes and Objects
classes_and_objects.description: Fundamental OOP structure where classes act as blueprints and objects are instances created with the new keyword.

constructors.name: Constructors
constructors.description: Special methods with the same name as the class that initialize objects and are invoked automatically upon creation.

encapsulation.name: Encapsulation
encapsulation.description: Hiding internal object state by using private fields and exposing behavior through public getters and setters.

access_modifiers.name: Access Modifiers
access_modifiers.description: Keywords like public, private, protected, and default that control visibility of class members.

inheritance.name: Inheritance
inheritance.description: Mechanism where a subclass acquires fields and methods from a superclass using the extends keyword.

polymorphism.name: Polymorphism
polymorphism.description: The ability of a method to be resolved at compile time (overloading) or runtime (overriding) based on context.

method_parameter_passing.name: Method Parameter Passing
method_parameter_passing.description: The rules governing how arguments are transferred to methods, specifically that Java is always pass-by-value.

abstraction.name: Abstraction
abstraction.description: Hiding complex implementation details by using abstract classes or interfaces to define behavior without detailing it.

interfaces.name: Java Interfaces
interfaces.description: Contracts that historically contained abstract methods but now support default, static, and private methods.

exception_handling.name: Exception Handling
exception_handling.description: The process of managing errors using checked/unchecked exceptions and control flow blocks like try, catch, and finally.

resource_management.name: Resource Management
resource_management.description: Techniques for automatically releasing resources like files, including the legacy finalize method and modern try-with-resources.

collections_and_generics.name: Collections and Generics
collections_and_generics.description: Java's library of data structures and the type system that enforces element types at compile time.

functional_java.name: Functional Java
functional_java.description: Modern syntax including lambda expressions and the Stream API for processing data declaratively.

modern_java_features.name: Modern Java Features
modern_java_features.description: Recent language enhancements such as local variable type inference with var, records, and sealed classes.

composition.name: Composition
composition.description: A design pattern using a has-a relationship to build complex objects from simpler parts, often preferred over inheritance.

claims.statement: In Java, a class serves as a blueprint for its objects, which are instantiated using the new keyword.
claims.quote: A class is a blueprint that defines the fields and methods of its objects, and an object is an instance of a class

claims.statement: All local variables in Java must have their data types explicitly declared.
claims.quote: In Java, every local variable must be declared with an explicit type, such as int count = 0 or String name

claims.statement: Constructors are automatically executed by the system whenever a new object instance is created.
claims.quote: A constructor has the same name as the class and runs automatically when an object is created.

claims.statement: Encapsulation is the practice of keeping object fields private and providing public methods to access or modify them.
claims.quote: Encapsulation hides the internal state of an object by making fields private and exposing public getter and setter methods.

claims.statement: Java provides four specific access modifiers to control the visibility of class members and methods.
claims.quote: Access modifiers in Java are public, protected, default (package-private) and private.

claims.statement: A Java class is restricted to extending only one other class, which prevents multiple inheritance of class implementation.
claims.quote: A Java class can extend only one class, so Java does not support multiple inheritance of classes.

claims.statement: Method overloading, where methods share a name but have different parameters, is a form of static polymorphism resolved by the compiler.
claims.quote: Method overloading means several methods in the same class share a name but have different parameter lists, and it is resolved at compile time.

claims.statement: Java transfers all method arguments by value, which results in a copy of the reference being passed for objects.
claims.quote: Java passes arguments by value; for objects, the value passed is a copy of the reference.

claims.statement: An abstract class in Java can contain both method definitions that must be implemented and concrete methods with full bodies.
claims.quote: An abstract class can have both abstract methods and concrete methods, and it cannot be instantiated.

claims.statement: According to basic definitions, a Java interface is limited to abstract methods and constants, with no implementation bodies allowed.
claims.quote: An interface in Java can contain only abstract methods and constants; it cannot contain any method body.

claims.statement: Implementing multiple interfaces allows a Java class to effectively achieve the benefits of multiple inheritance.
claims.quote: A class can implement several interfaces, which is how Java achieves a form of multiple inheritance.

claims.statement: Checked exceptions must be handled by the programmer either through a catch block or by declaring them in the throws clause.
claims.quote: Checked exceptions must be either caught or declared with throws, while unchecked exceptions extend RuntimeException.

claims.statement: The finalize method was traditionally used to ensure resources were released by the garbage collector.
claims.quote: To release resources such as files, override the finalize() method so the garbage collector closes them.

claims.statement: Using Java generics in collections allows the compiler to perform type checking and eliminate the need for downcasting.
claims.quote: Generics such as List<String> let the compiler check element types and avoid casts.

claims.statement: Java 8 updated the language to allow interfaces to define methods with implementation bodies, known as default methods.
claims.quote: Since Java 8, interfaces can contain default methods and static methods with a body, in addition to abstract methods.

claims.statement: The introduction of the var keyword in Java 10 allows developers to write local variables without explicitly stating their types.
claims.quote: Since Java 10, the var keyword lets the compiler infer the type of a local variable, as in var names

claims.statement: The finalize method has been deprecated and is slated for removal due to being unpredictable and causing performance issues.
claims.quote: The finalize() method was deprecated in Java 9 and deprecated for removal in Java 18, because finalizers are unpredictable and slow.

claims.statement: Designers should prefer composition over inheritance when dealing with has-a relationships between objects.
claims.quote: Favour composition over inheritance when classes have a has-a relationship rather than an is-a relationship.

claims.statement: Java uses pass-by-value, meaning object references are copied to the method scope rather than passed by reference.
claims.quote: Java is always pass-by-value: when an object is passed to a method, the method receives a copy of the reference.

claims.statement: Lambda expressions, available since Java 8, allow for passing functional logic directly as arguments to methods.
claims.quote: Lambda expressions, introduced in Java 8, let you pass behaviour as an argument, for example list.forEach(x -> System.out.println(x)).

claims.statement: Java records, introduced in Java 16, automatically provide boilerplate code like constructors, accessors, and hashing methods for immutable data.
claims.quote: Records, standard since Java 16, are concise immutable data classes that generate the constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode and toString.

claims.statement: A source claims that Java allows a single class to inherit from two or more parent classes.
claims.quote: Java supports multiple inheritance of classes, so a class can extend two parent classes at once.

claims.statement: A source asserts that Java objects are passed by reference, allowing methods to alter the caller's variable.
claims.quote: Java is pass-by-reference for objects, so assigning a new object to a parameter also changes the caller's variable.

claims.statement: A source argues that inheritance is universally superior to composition for code reuse and minimizing the amount of code typed.
claims.quote: Inheritance is always better than composition because it lets you reuse code with less typing.

claims.statement: A source suggests that string comparisons should use the equals operator due to performance benefits over the equals method.
claims.quote: Always compare strings with == because it is faster than equals().

claims.statement: Java developers are required to have a strong understanding of fundamental OOP principles like encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism.
claims.quote: Strong grasp of object-oriented design: encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and interfaces.

claims.statement: Proficiency in modern Java functional features, such as lambdas and the Stream API, is required for certain roles.
claims.quote: Modern Java features, including lambdas, the Stream API and records for immutable data.

claims.statement: Candidates must be familiar with handling exceptions and using try-with-resources for safe code execution.
claims.quote: Exception handling and safe resource management with try-with-resources.

claims.statement: Knowledge of Java's Collections framework and the use of generics is a required skill for backend engineering roles.
claims.quote: Good knowledge of the Collections framework and generics.

claims.statement: Engineers are expected to design class hierarchies that utilize interfaces with default methods and prefer composition where applicable.
claims.quote: Designing class hierarchies with interfaces, including default methods, and favouring composition where it fits.

claims.statement: It is required that software engineers understand the specific rule that Java passes object references by value.
claims.quote: Understanding that Java passes object references by value when debugging method calls.

claims.statement: Familiarity with current Java syntax, specifically the use of var and records, is a required skill for developers.
claims.quote: Familiarity with modern Java syntax such as var and records.

prerequisites.reason: Features like records are syntax enhancements built on top of existing class structures.
Inheritance is a mechanism that links two classes.
Exceptions in Java are objects, and try-catch blocks manage them within class methods.
Access modifiers control the visibility of members within a class.
Collections are class libraries and generics enforce types for object arrays.
Constructors are defined within classes and executed when objects are instantiated.
Abstraction is realized using abstract classes and methods.
Encapsulation relies on classes to group fields and requires access modifiers to hide state.
Runtime polymorphism (method overriding) specifically depends on the inheritance hierarchy.
The concept of interfaces is often taught alongside inheritance to explain how to achieve multiple type implementation.
Composition is a design alternative that contrasts with inheritance for code reuse.
Understanding how object references are passed by value helps explain how method calls are resolved and interact with objects.
Interfaces are a form of abstraction that define contracts for classes to implement.
Lambda expressions implement functional interfaces like Supplier and Consumer.
Modern resource management using try-with-resources directly relies on exception handling syntax.
The Stream API and many lambda expressions operate directly on collection frameworks, so collections must be understood.
